name: Mutualism
summary: Mutualism is an anarchist school of socialism that wants an economy of artisans, small producers and workers' cooperatives exchanging goods at labour cost, with occupancy-and-use property rights and credit issued by democratic mutual banks. It attacks rent, profit and interest as exploitation, and wants government replaced by contracts and federations of free groups, reached gradually.
scope: The profile follows Pierre-Joseph Proudhon (What Is Property?, General Idea of the Revolution, The Principle of Federation) and the American mutualists Josiah Warren, William B. Greene and Benjamin Tucker's labour-and-usury analysis. It excludes collectivist and communist anarchism, and Proudhon's views on women and family are treated as split because later mutualists rejected them.

keyFigures.name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
keyFigures.role: Formulated mutualism as a comprehensive economic theory and proposed the People's Bank.

keyFigures.name: Josiah Warren
keyFigures.role: American anarchist who ran the Cincinnati Time Store on equitable commerce and labour notes.

keyFigures.name: William Batchelder Greene
keyFigures.role: Developed mutual banking and labour-value theory in the United States.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Proudhon would have localities care for their own invalids rather than a central state pay for them, and mutualists favour voluntary mutual aid over tax-funded state provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A legal wage floor is state wage-setting; mutualists aim to end wage exploitation through cost-priced exchange and mutual credit, not by decree.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mutualists call their model an anti-capitalist free market with exchange at cost, and Tucker held that free competition would erase usury, though they reject capitalist markets resting on state privilege.

public-ownership.rationale: Proudhon rejected the state even as administrative servant and called state-run banks and similar schemes new channels of parasitism; ownership belongs to users and associations.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proudhon aimed to abolish taxation through near-free credit and to abolish the land tax, so raising taxes is not the mutualist way to curb wealth; they attack rent, interest and profit at source.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' self-management and free association are core principles, so worker organisations are welcomed, although mutualists emphasise cooperatives and mutual credit more than trade-union bargaining.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mutualist property is conditional on occupancy and use, and Proudhon wanted property dissolved and reconstituted, so titles may be overridden when they enable exploitation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mutualists want the state-granted monopolies behind large concentrated capital abolished rather than tightly managed by the state, so more regulation is not their remedy.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mutualists oppose state programmes but blame poverty on rent, interest and profit rather than on dependency; adherents would cut the state while stressing mutual aid, which this statement does not capture. Inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mutualism favours workers' control, with workers' cooperatives alongside artisans and sole proprietors, so collective worker ownership is one accepted form rather than the only one.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; inferred from Proudhon's hostility to government, police and security in the service of property.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Tucker-style liberty and Proudhon's view that a free society needs no prohibitory state, though Proudhon was personally austere.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from opposition to state coercion and the 'alegal' ideal of a society with no state-made prohibitions.

strong-leader.rationale: Proudhon wrote that the history of governments is the martyrology of the proletariat and that the choice is Government or No-government, rejecting dictatorship and personal rule outright.

state-harmful.rationale: Proudhon's stated revolutionary aim is 'No Government', with authority in principle and government in practice replaced by economic contracts.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; Proudhon wanted arms under local control and a citizenry rather than central armies, and mutualists distrust state bans, so adherents lean against strict state limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proudhon saw the state's police as a protector of the rich and wanted soldiers and arms under local control, federalised only in wartime.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Proudhon was a moralist while individualists like Tucker favoured liberty, so adherents are split. Inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Proudhon's federal principle gives execution to local and provincial authorities, with the centre only initiating and supervising.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Proudhon's reciprocity principle and his criticism of punishments imposed by a ruling state.

traditional-family.rationale: Proudhon was strongly patriarchal and treated the family as a social foundation, yet he saw it as the origin of monarchical authority and other mutualists differ, so adherents are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon was socially conservative but the 'alegal' ideal removes state control of marriage, and later mutualists differ.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Proudhon-era mutualists and later individualists diverge on this.

more-religion-public.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools, like churches, strictly separated from the state and treated religion as a private matter of reasoned judgment.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists opposed slavery and coercion generally but did not propose state redress, so the answer is inferred and split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Proudhon held fixed sex roles while later libertarian mutualists did not, so adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Proudhon criticised indivisible national unity as a myth and favoured federations of regions, so national culture is not a mutualist priority; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Gradualism is listed among mutualism's key principles, built through mutual banks and cooperatives, though Proudhon did not defer to established institutions like the state.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from federal, anti-statist principles that distrust state border controls.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Proudhon wanted limited federal pacts whose authority rests on members' consent, not a stronger central body; supranational power would be a new government.

free-trade.rationale: Tucker named tariffs one of the four monopolies and wanted exchange free of state privilege, though mutualists tie exchange to cost.

nation-first.rationale: Proudhon's federalism proposed pacts limited to mutual defence and benefit and favoured general disarmament, so national self-assertion is not a mutualist aim; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; federations are not built for conquest in Proudhon's view and mutualists oppose state military power, so adherents lean against intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from free association and hostility to state sovereignty over movement.

limit-growth.rationale: Not discussed by these sources; mutualists aim to organise production around workers' needs and cost, and have no growth-limiting programme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists distrust state action but accept collective responses, so the position is inferred and split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated mutualist view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated view, and adherents would judge it by local control rather than by the state.

revolution-justified.rationale: Proudhon wrote of a general idea of the revolution, though he sought it through economic organisation and peaceful transformation rather than violence, so only mild agreement.

experts-over-public.rationale: Proudhon scorned both government by officials and direct legislation but wanted economic self-organisation by producers, so adherents reject rule by experts; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Proudhon wanted 'the organization of economic forces' by producers' contracts and rejected state direction of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualists accept markets with exchange at cost among workers' cooperatives and artisans, in line with this statement, though they reject public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Proudhon wanted the land tax abolished and land held by users, so a single tax on land value is not the mutualist route, although they share the aim of ending rent.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; mutualists oppose unearned income yet reject taxation as a state tool, so adherents are split.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional state payments would be a government transfer, which mutualists reject in favour of cost-priced exchange and mutual credit.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tucker listed tariffs among the four state monopolies that shelter profit from competition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proudhon rejected state-run banks and state direction of capital; investment should come from mutual credit.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mutualists aim for an economy of artisans, small holders and cooperatives without concentrated land or capital, and Tucker said ending usury would spread wealth widely.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mutualism keeps money (in mutual-bank notes) and ends exploitative wage labour through self-management, but does not abolish money or exchange.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Mutualists want credit issued by competing mutual banks and attack the banking monopoly, though they want users to own banks, not a market left alone.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Proudhon rejected state-recognised bodies setting wages and prices; mutualist exchange is by free contract at cost.

one-party-rule.rationale: Proudhon's aim is 'No Government' and he held that the history of governments is the martyrology of the proletariat, which excludes a ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Proudhon stated the real choice in 1850 was not monarchy or republic but government or no government, and treated authority as the source of oppression.

democracy-best.rationale: Proudhon called universal suffrage a lottery and attacked direct government as an absurdity, preferring contract and federation to majority rule.

direct-votes.rationale: Proudhon called direct legislation one of the biggest blunders in politics and the reduction to absurdity of the governmental idea.

workers-councils.rationale: Proudhon rejected parliaments and wanted economic organisation to absorb government, but did not propose councils as political power; adherents are split.

right-to-secede.rationale: Proudhon's universal federalism gives self-governing groups a right of secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rejects authority in principle; mutualists hold no one is naturally entitled to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mutualists pursue gradual, peaceful change through banks and cooperatives, but Proudhon and others did not renounce all violence; inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Proudhon wanted federations limited to defence and proposed general disarmament, and saw militarism as the tool of centralised states.

separate-church-state.rationale: Proudhon argued that schools, like churches, should be strictly separated from the state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Proudhon wanted one law of reciprocity based on contract, not scripture; he was anti-clerical.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Tucker favoured private defence and courts, while Proudhon wanted federated local bodies and justice delegated by citizens; adherents are split.

military-superiority.rationale: Proudhon favoured general disarmament and federation limited to defence, rejecting great-power rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Proudhon rejected the myth of indivisible national unity in favour of confederations of regions.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mutualists see classes as exploiting through rent, interest and profit, but Proudhon sought reciprocity, not class war as history's driver; split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mutualists want each to receive the full product of their labour at cost, which differs by work, rather than equal results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; occupancy-and-use titles would favour those who use the land, but no stated position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists reject state transfers, so adherents lean against, while opposing colonialism itself; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Proudhon favoured regional federations by free contract rather than blocs defined by civilisation; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mutualists mix reciprocity and mutual aid with self-ownership of labour, so they do not simply endorse self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Proudhon held that obligation arises only from free undertaking, and rejected communal duties imposed on individuals.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated mutualist view.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; no stated mutualist view.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mutualists favour industry organised by cooperatives, not abandonment; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; no stated mutualist view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Proudhon's rejection of government by any rulers, human or mechanical.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from liberty-first individualism that distrusts state access to private affairs.

restore-past-order.rationale: Proudhon sought a new organisation (reconstituting property, credit and society) rather than restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Proudhon grounded his programme in reciprocity as principle rather than judging policy case by case; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Mutualists build alternatives (mutual banks, cooperatives, the Cincinnati Time Store) rather than relying on elections; Proudhon dismissed voting.

means-match-ends.rationale: Mutualism's gradualism builds the future society in mutual institutions now, as with Proudhon's People's Bank and Warren's labour exchanges.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Mutualists favour artisans and cooperatives working with machines and exchange, not primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mutualists accept specialised trades exchanging at cost; they would reorganise labour under self-management, not abolish division.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mutualism holds the labour theory of value and price equal to labour cost, so goods go by work, not need.

production-for-use.rationale: Mutualists want exchange at cost with no profit, which in effect aims production at use, but they keep markets; low because they do not frame it this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mutualists oppose profit, rent and non-nominal interest as forms of labour exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Proudhon's formula of 'No Government' rejects any dictatorship, including a working-class one.

collective-farming.rationale: Proudhon wanted farmland to pass to those who use it, with owner-occupiers keeping title, not collective farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mutualists blame state-backed monopoly, which may include war, but there is no stated view.

taxation-theft.rationale: Individualist mutualists such as Tucker treat state levies as coercive and Proudhon sought to abolish taxation, though the 'theft' framing is not central.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from Tucker-style equal liberty, with Proudhon's reciprocity; the principle is not stated in these terms.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Proudhon's federation gives groups sovereignty and rights of secession while contract rests on individuals; mutualists are split.

conscription.rationale: Proudhon wanted arms and soldiers under local control and rejected central military power.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Proudhon dismissed voting as a lottery and made obligation depend on free undertaking, with the right to leave a federation.

state-as-business.rationale: Proudhon called the swollen state a vast limited company crushing citizens, but mutualists reject the state itself, not just its business model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mutualists want credit and access to land and tools so workers can act freely, which implies material means, but this is not stated as such.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; no stated mutualist view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; mutualism's equality of exchange and opposition to privilege makes adherents reject racial hierarchy; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Proudhon rejected political representation by government, but wanted producers' economic federations to replace it; inferred as split towards trade bodies, leaning no.

total-state.rationale: Proudhon's stated goal is 'No Government', the opposite of a state directing every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not discussed; Proudhon rejected nationalist unity in favour of federation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Proudhon held federations are not built for conquest and proposed disarmament.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Proudhon condemned feudal, governmental practices and made obligation depend on free contract.

bound-labor.rationale: Proudhon called interest and rent feudal practices and wanted land to pass to those who work it.

universal-morality.rationale: Proudhon grounded society in reciprocity, 'do to others as you would they should do to you', as a universal principle, but this is about justice not metaphysics.

single-common-good.rationale: Proudhon treated liberty and authority as irreducible opposing principles and favoured balance through federation over a single imposed good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic; mutualists reject state-building in general and Proudhon opposed national unity, so inferred as lean against.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists reject state-imposed national unity, so a state language revival is not their aim; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' self-management is a core mutualist principle, though the statement includes the public and large companies, which mutualists would replace with cooperatives.

school-vouchers.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools separate from the state, but vouchers keep the state paying; adherents are split. Inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Proudhon opposed state banks and state-driven finance, so government stimulus spending is not mutualist; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Tucker held that liberty alone could end usury, tying political and economic freedom together.

rule-by-example.rationale: Mutualists reject rulers altogether rather than relying on their moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Proudhon's universal federalism gives self-governing groups a right of secession, though groups are not necessarily nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Proudhon wanted federations limited to defence and rejected militarism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Proudhon was an anti-clerical rationalist, though Greene presented mutualism as the religion of the coming age, so mild.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Mutualists reject state welfare; local self-care by communities is preferred, so no state preference for citizens either; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Mutualists oppose state welfare and unearned income and expect work; the specific conditionality is not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Proudhon sought reciprocity between producers by contract rather than class war, though he also attacked capitalists as parasitic.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Proudhon sought a new social organisation but did not call for destroying culture; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Not discussed; Proudhon preferred voluntary federal pacts to blocs, with no stated view on this.

workers-nation.rationale: Proudhon opposed national unity as a myth and favoured federated producers' associations, not national classes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Proudhon held strongly to distinct roles, but Tucker and Greene did not; the anarchist 'alegal' ideal rules out law doing so, so adherents split with Proudhon the core.

ban-interest.rationale: Proudhon wanted interest cut to cover administrative costs and eventually ended by competing mutual credit, not forbidden by law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rejects state-made prohibitions and legal privilege generally.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Proudhon described the state as an instrument protecting the property of the rich against the poor, and Tucker called it the protector of usury.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; no mutualist position on energy sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Proudhon opposed enforced national unity, so forced assimilation fits poorly; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in mutualist sources; adherents blame state-backed monopoly, not demographic plots.

proportional-representation.rationale: Proudhon called universal suffrage a lottery and rejected parliaments; proportional seat allocation would still be government by representatives.

national-mission.rationale: Proudhon rejected conquest and national unity, so a mission to spread a form of government is foreign to mutualism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Proudhon defended patriarchal family order while Tucker and others opposed sex inequality, so the answer is split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Proudhon wrote that governments are the martyrology of the proletariat and that the state shields the propertied, so distrust of political elites is central.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rejects state coercion over families as part of the opposition to authority.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists distrust police and army but have no stated view on legal accountability for past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Proudhon rejected the state even as an administrative servant, so a limited state is still too much, though Tucker-style adherents would accept defence by voluntary means.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: State discouragement of private choices is contrary to mutualist liberty; Proudhon's equal reciprocity does not support racial hierarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Reciprocity between persons as equals is the basis of Proudhon's contract, though 'equal rights before the law' conflicts with his rejection of state law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no mutualist counterpart.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; no stated mutualist view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Proudhon wanted a single contract-based law of reciprocity but no state codes; the question is not addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Proudhon wanted religion separated from the state and treated belief as a matter of reasoned judgment.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from rejection of state-made prohibitions.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Proudhon argued that schools, like churches, should be strictly separated from the state.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Proudhon's aim is 'No Government' and the state should dissolve into the economic organism, not grow under threat.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Proudhon described federal authority as resting on the consent of the members, and held that obligation arises only from free undertaking.

trade-surplus.rationale: Tucker opposed tariffs and state trade policy; mutualists aim at exchange at cost, not surpluses; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Rejects coercive state action against persons as contrary to contract and reciprocity.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Tucker's equal-liberty position bars aggression, though Proudhon did not state it as an absolute and accepted revolution.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Tucker praised free competition as ending usury, but mutualists stress reciprocity and mutual aid over struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Rejects state suppression of political organising; Proudhon himself was prosecuted, though he also sought to dissolve the constitutional order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Proudhon's rejection of authority and the wage relationship, and Tucker's condemnation of coercion, fit a view that dependence on another's power is unfreedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Proudhon wanted federal division of power but also no government; adherents are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Proudhon rejected government and authority including a ruling party, and held that workers' organisation comes through economic association.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Mutualism aims to free workers from exploitation but does not give priority by law; low.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Proudhon proposed that rent payments count towards ownership, so tenants gradually become owners; inferred sympathy for the principle.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Free association among workers is a mutualist principle, so legal restrictions on strikes are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Proudhon blamed rent, interest and the property system for poverty, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon favoured federal pluralism, so adherents lean against.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Proudhon called universal suffrage a lottery as a criticism, yet wanted no government; no stated view on lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Contradicts Proudhon's hostility to government power and his reciprocity principle.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices should be set by cost and competition, not state caps; Tucker held state interference caused scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: Proudhon's 'No Government' excludes government or party control of the press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Proudhon wanted arms under local control, federalised only in wartime, not a party's army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from federal free association.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Proudhon rejected representation itself, so the question of pay is not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Proudhon held that a minority is not bound by majority decisions it did not consent to.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Proudhon favoured federation by free contract among self-governing units, but a state-run union like the EU is not the same thing; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Proudhon rejected concentrated personal command of the army and government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Proudhon was anti-clerical and wanted churches separated from the state; church governance is a private matter.

clerical-rule.rationale: Proudhon wanted churches separated from the state and rejected any authority in government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Proudhon opposed war and militarism, and later mutualists were anti-war, but this internationalist stance is a socialist-wide position rather than stated mutualism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Proudhon was a moralist but rejected governmental prohibition of expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rejects the presidency as an office of authority, so the statement's premise is opposed.

recall-officials.rationale: Proudhon wanted delegates bound by their contracts; he rejected representation but would hold any officials to those contracts.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Proudhon wanted federations limited to defence and general disarmament, so permanent alliances and troops abroad are contrary.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Proudhon called rent speculation and wanted rent to build tenant ownership, but did not ban renting outright.

people-in-arms.rationale: Proudhon wanted arms under local control rather than central armies.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Proudhon opposed the ideal of indivisible national unity in favour of federal groupings.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Proudhon's federal pluralism implies respect for differing groups, but no explicit statement.

death-penalty.rationale: Proudhon opposed it in the 1848 era and mutualists rejected state violence; not covered in the sources I opened.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools separated from the state, and sex education goes unaddressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools separate from the state like churches, so the state should teach no creed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Proudhon was moralist but opposed prohibition by government; split with Tucker libertarianism, leaning no.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; federal membership by contract rather than blood.

minority-language-support.rationale: Federal pluralism implies local cultural autonomy, but state support is not mutualist; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Mutualists reject general state laws burdening beliefs, but Proudhon had little sympathy for religion; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not stated in the sources; inferred from individualist liberty among later mutualists, while Proudhon himself was a moralist.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Proudhon wanted interest abolished, but sovereign debts are not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Proudhon held that political change without economic organisation was empty, since the economic organism should absorb government.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Proudhon criticised assemblies and universal suffrage; a contract between groups replaces constitution making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inconsistent with the mutualist rejection of authority.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mutualists favour mutual aid, but state-to-state aid is not addressed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Proudhon proposed general disarmament and rejected militarism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rejects the office of head of state and called universal suffrage a lottery.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Mutualists oppose any central monopoly of money and want credit issued by competing mutual banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon rejected nationalist territorial claims, so adherents lean against.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Proudhon distinguished property tied to labour, which he defended, from property tied to coercion; conditions are use-based rather than on the common good as such.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mutualists held that state ownership recreates exploitation, so anarchists regard state socialism as state capitalism; the claim is not stated in the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the sources; no stated mutualist view on environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Proudhon wanted federations limited to mutual defence, which is close, but wanted no standing alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Consent of a people to its membership of a federation follows from Proudhon's contract principle; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Proudhon wanted church and state separate, not the state placing clergy under authority.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Proudhon's universal federalism includes a right of secession, so force is rejected.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Federal pacts leave members more rights than they cede, so regions keep their own systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Proudhon called authority and government oppressive and was an anti-clerical rationalist.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Proudhon wanted taxation abolished in favour of near-free credit, so an income tax of any shape is not mutualist.

character-from-environment.rationale: Proudhon argued that property and institutions shape workers' condition, but the sources do not take a stand on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Proudhon rejected any ruler's authority and held the law of reciprocity binds all.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Proudhon wanted federal balance of liberty and authority, but rejected rule by few or many.

leader-cult.rationale: Proudhon's attack on authority and government rejects personal cults of rulers.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no mutualist counterpart.

land-redistribution.rationale: Proudhon wanted farmland to pass to those who work it, though by gradual transformation of rent into ownership rather than by seizure.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the right of free association and occupancy-and-use title.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Proudhon rejected the myth of national unity and conquest.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Proudhon held belief is a matter of reasoned judgment and wanted church and state separate.

women-must-cover.rationale: Rejects state coercion of personal conduct.

common-currency.rationale: Mutualists favour competing mutual-bank money; a shared state currency is not addressed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Proudhon rejected unity as a myth and favoured federation by free contract.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Federal pluralism supports self-governing cultural groups; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Proudhon stressed economic forces yet also ideas of justice and reciprocity; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Tucker attacked monopolies and wanted competition to end privileged concentrations, but via removal of state privilege, not state prohibition; mild.

no-bailouts.rationale: Mutualists oppose state support for banks, since the banking monopoly is a state privilege.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Proudhon rejected majority rule and held that a minority is not bound by decisions it did not consent to.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Tucker favoured free trade against tariffs, and Proudhon rejected closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists reject state trade policy but favour fair exchange.

moral-incentives.rationale: Mutualists reward work by price equal to labour cost, not moral exhortation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mutualists favour gradual building of alternatives, not insurrection by a small group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Proudhon attacked feudal rent, interest and privilege as products of government.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mutualists reject rule by others without consent.

patriotic-education.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools separated from state and rejected national unity as myth.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists oppose state privilege but also do not address this.

public-money-creation.rationale: Proudhon rejected state-run banks as channels of parasitism and wanted credit issued by mutual banks.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Mutualists argue that rent, interest and profit by their nature exploit labour and must be abolished, so capitalism's crises are inherent.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Proudhon rejected conquest and imperial influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Tucker favoured free trade; not addressed otherwise.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Mutualists see all wage labour as exploited by rent, interest and profit; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Tucker-style equal liberty favours free association, but Proudhon and Greene did not discuss it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Proudhon rejected constitutions imposed by a state but wanted reciprocal rights by contract; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; federal consent principle suggests agreements need the consent of those bound, but no stated position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Proudhon wanted no rulers, and called universal suffrage a lottery, so choosing rulers by election is not the answer.

minority-veto.rationale: Proudhon held that a minority is not bound by majority decisions it did not consent to, because obligation arises only from free undertaking.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Proudhon's revolutionary stance supports resisting rulers, but mutualists would remove the ruler's office altogether, not restore constitutional rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Proudhon rejected parliamentary lawmaking and wanted a single law of reciprocity and economic contract.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Mutualists reject an owning class living off rent and interest and then giving charity; justice by reciprocity replaces duty by privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Proudhon dismissed voting and government yet organised economic action, so adherents reject politics in the state sense but not social activity.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Proudhon stressed the state's protection of property, not cultural consent; no stated view.

native-born-offices.rationale: Proudhon wanted no government offices as authority and rejected nationalist exclusivity.

party-own-road.rationale: Mutualists reject central direction by any party or foreign centre, but the statement is about communist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mutualists favour self-organised credit and exchange among producers rather than external loans; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Proudhon rejected nationalist territorial claims and conquest.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; mutualist federalism opposes political rule over others by any descent group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Mutualists oppose authoritarian government, but constitutions are not their instrument; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Proudhon's rejection of authority condemns both, but the equivalence framing is not discussed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Proudhon's federalism leaves each group to organise itself, but this is about forms of government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Proudhon wanted military power under local control and federalised only in wartime, not as a political guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists hold that labour should receive its product, but Proudhon saw women's role differently.

filial-duty.rationale: Proudhon held patriarchal family values, but no stated position here.

office-by-exam.rationale: Proudhon rejected government offices; no stated view on how they would be filled.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Tucker opposed state barriers to trade and exchange; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Proudhon opposed divorce for women's autonomy while others differ; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Proudhon wanted representatives bound by their contracts, though he rejected representation itself.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Mutual banks and mutual aid societies could provide pensions, but the statement leaves private companies; no stated view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mutualist land titles are conditional on occupancy and use, and land is not a commodity.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Proudhon wanted taxation abolished and rejected parliaments, so there is no stated position.

single-official-language.rationale: Proudhon's federalism rejects enforced uniformity, so adherents lean against.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Occupancy-and-use title applies regardless of nationality, though no stated view.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Proudhon rejected conquest and wanted general disarmament.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Proudhon held that federations rest on the consent of members who may leave.

corporate-influence.rationale: Proudhon held government serves the propertied, and Tucker held the state protects monopolies, so corporate influence on government is central to the critique.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Rejects state restriction of voluntary exchange and association.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Proudhon rejected state transfers and taxation.

residents-only-property.rationale: Occupancy-and-use titles favour those who live and work on land, so residents-only limits fit.

job-guarantee.rationale: Proudhon sought the guaranty of work and wages as a revolutionary aim but through mutual credit and exchange, not the state as employer.

democratic-peace.rationale: Proudhon rejected democracy as the answer, but this is a descriptive claim not addressed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Proudhon held that obligation arises only from free undertaking and that a minority is not bound by laws it did not consent to.

non-intervention.rationale: Proudhon's federation rests on the consent of members, so outside intervention is illegitimate; 'for any reason' makes it mild.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy claim; Proudhon's era of antisemitism aside, mutualist principles of reciprocity do not support it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 'alegal' ideal removes state benefits, but Proudhon held strongly to marriage; split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Proudhon wanted transparency through contract and economic organisation, but this is not stated.

local-production.rationale: Proudhon's federation and local execution favour local organisation of production; mutualists also exchange across distance at cost.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mutualists build free associations and local exchanges rather than hierarchical parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Proudhon wanted federal pacts over national supremacy, but also no centralised international authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Proudhon wanted churches separate from the state and rejected national unity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejects hierarchical relations among states and conquest.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Federal pacts leave members more rights than they cede, including local control of resources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mutualists defend personal property in the product of one's labour, including what one needs for personal use.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mutualists reject state communism but also oppose state suppression; coexistence is the likely stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Proudhon rejected state-funded services, preferring local and mutual provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Proudhon was an anti-theist but Greene saw mutualism as the religion of the coming age; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Proudhon recognised that the capitalist period organised collective labour but condemned its exploitation; split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Proudhon opposed female equality, while later mutualists such as Tucker and Greene supported it; split.

socialized-care.rationale: Mutualists reject state provision and Proudhon defended the family; Proudhon opposed socialising housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Proudhon's federalism opposes state imposition of a purified language; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Proudhon's federation rests on contract among parties, whose terms bind until agreed otherwise.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mutualists favour cooperatives and free association, but the property is held by individuals or associations by occupancy and use, not necessarily communal.

majority-settlement.rationale: Rejects state-organised settlement and ethnic engineering.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Mutualism is an anti-capitalist free market that also rejects state communism; Proudhon called property theft and also defended possession.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Mutualist land title rests on occupancy and use rather than historical or religious ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A factual claim with no support in mutualist sources.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Proudhon was personally hostile, but mutualists oppose state prohibitions; split, leaning no.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Proudhon's 'No Government' rejects state suppression; he was himself imprisoned for opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Proudhon wanted church and state separate and belief a matter of reasoned judgment.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Proudhon rejected conquest and rule over other peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists oppose religious obligation imposed by law.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Proudhon wanted church separate from state, rejecting rule by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Proudhon rejected direct government and voting but wanted workers to run their own affairs by contract in workplaces; the statement is about decisions, not government.

alienated-labor.rationale: Proudhon held wage labour enclosed the value of collective work and that workers were robbed of their product, close to alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A cultural claim contrary to mutualist reciprocity and federal pluralism; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Proudhon held authority is the principle of government and the root of oppression.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Proudhon's separation of church and state favours neutrality, so public officials wearing religious dress; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists favour free contract but oppose coerced silence; no stated view.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mutualists want an anti-capitalist market without the state's social-protection apparatus, using mutual aid and credit instead.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Proudhon proposed general disarmament and local control of arms, though he allowed defence in wartime.

rich-first.rationale: Mutualists aim to end exploitation by rent, interest and profit rather than let some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Proudhon wanted federations limited to mutual defence and rejected great-power rivalry.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Proudhon treated the family as the origin of monarchical authority and rejected hereditary rule as government in principle.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualists propose democratically run mutual banks issuing credit at nominal interest, as in Proudhon's Bank of the People and Greene's mutual banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Proudhon wanted interest cut and credit freed from moneylenders; inferred sympathy for refusing conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Proudhon called universal suffrage a lottery but opposed privilege; a property franchise gives power to owners, which he condemned.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Proudhon held that government and property serve the rich, so rights alone are hollow without economic equality, as in his demand for economic reorganisation.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Proudhon rejected state laws and wanted a single law of reciprocity; split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Proudhon rejected privileged voting and treated persons as equals in contract.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Proudhon rejected direct legislation and voting.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Proudhon wanted church and state separate and belief a private matter.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mutualists favour free association but reject targeting a group; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Proudhon rejected assemblies and direct government; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon held religion a private matter.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Mutualists aim to build an economy without capital accumulation or concentrated land ownership, and Tucker saw the monopolies as destroying labour's liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Proudhon was anti-clerical but wanted the state out of schools and belief; state promotion is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Proudhon saw police as protecting property, but Tucker favoured private defence and courts; mutualists replace the state's police with local or voluntary arrangements.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Federal pacts fit but this is a state-level arrangement; no stated view.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mutualists prefer voluntary mutual aid over state programmes, though they reject charity as a substitute for justice.

term-limits.rationale: Proudhon rejected representation altogether; no stated view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Proudhon rejected voting and direct government; no stated view.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Proudhon defended the husband's authority while Tucker and Greene differ; split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Proudhon rejected voting; no stated view.

rent-control.rationale: Proudhon called rent speculation and wanted it ended by converting payments into ownership, not capped by law.

abolish-ip.rationale: Tucker named patents among the four monopolies, and mutualists apply the cost principle against intellectual monopolies.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rejects militarism and nationalist training of youth.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Proudhon wanted arms under local control and defensive-only federations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Mutualists hold the labour theory of value and oppose rent, profit and interest as forms of exploitation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Tucker and the mutualists accept defence of persons against force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Proudhon rejected the myth of national unity and continuity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Proudhon rejected national cults and militarism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Proudhon treated politics as economic and juridical; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Proudhon wanted no state; no stated view on cultural renewal.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Reciprocity and free competition by contract apply regardless of group membership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Proudhon opposed the unity ideal in favour of federated regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Free association of workers outside the state is a mutualist principle.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Mutualists want workers' self-management and control of production, though not through a political state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Proudhon wanted towns to take over housing and rural policing, close to local services, but mutualists prefer mutual and cooperative ownership to public.

second-chamber.rationale: Rejects legislatures, so adding a chamber is opposed; low.

municipal-property.rationale: Proudhon wanted towns as collective owners of housing and farmland for use by occupiers, though mutualists emphasise individual possession.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Proudhon's federal principle makes the central body only initiate, set general rules and supervise while locals govern.

family-wage.rationale: Proudhon argued wages should support a family, but later mutualists did not; split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state regulatory barriers.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Rejects tax-funded state research as such; low.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Mutualist mutual banks issuing their own currency outside the state monopoly fit this aim.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from liberty and opposition to state surveillance.

person-over-state.rationale: Proudhon held the state exists to protect propertied interests, not people, and that authority must be limited by liberty.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Greene's mutualism had a religious dimension but Proudhon was anti-theist; split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Proudhon's federal pacts leave members more rights than they give up, so a central legislature cannot withdraw them.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mutualism's equal exchange by contract does not organise by race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Proudhon held that federal pacts are limited to mutual defence and shared benefit and proposed disarmament.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Proudhon rejected nationalist unity in favour of regional federations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Proudhon rejected voting and parliaments; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no support in mutualist sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Proudhon wanted schools separate from the state, and tax-funded provision is opposed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Proudhon sought abolition of taxation; liability by contract fits better than a state tax.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Proudhon held fixed distinct roles while others differ; no stated view.

arms-reduction.rationale: Proudhon proposed general disarmament as a goal of federation.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Proudhon's pacts are by consent and public contract; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Tucker opposed state control of money and trade.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Proudhon wanted arms under local control and federalised only in wartime, not a state monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Proudhon opposed militarism and wars of conquest.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Free association of workers and employers by contract fits mutualist method, though cooperatives aim to end the employer-worker divide.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proudhon sought abolition of taxation and wages set by exchange.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Mutualists reject state borrowing but not by legal rules; no stated view.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Proudhon wanted the political system dissolved into the economic organisation, not captured, though gradually.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Mutualism's gradualist, voluntary approach lets communities try mutual banks, labour notes and cooperatives, with no fixed blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Mutualists regard land as not a commodity, so counting nature as capital is opposed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Proudhon rejected national unity as a myth.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Proudhon sought abolition of interest on debts, but not by state relief; split.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Proudhon criticised centralisation but not in these terms; no stated view.

public-service-media.rationale: Rejects state funding and control of media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Greene's esoteric view suggests it, but Proudhon rejected religion; split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Proudhon wanted farmers freed from moneylenders by mutual credit and ownership of land, not state price guarantees.

workers-own-party.rationale: Proudhon rejected parties and political action in favour of economic association.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Proudhon opposed it but Tucker supported; split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Tucker-style liability for harm to others' property applies; inferred from equal liberty.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; liberty-first individualists would reject.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Proudhon rejected state punishment and law; fixed sentences are state-imposed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Proudhon's federalism rejects uniform state demands.

voter-id.rationale: Proudhon dismissed voting, so does not support rules for it; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Proudhon wanted state and church separated, so no interpretation holds legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Proudhon rejected democracy as a form of government and called universal suffrage a lottery; no stated view on the definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Proudhon's moralism and Tucker's liberty differ; split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Proudhon rejected state transfers and taxation.

women-suffrage.rationale: Proudhon opposed women's suffrage, and also rejected voting itself; other mutualists differ.

missingStatements.text: The price of goods and services should equal the labour cost of producing them.
missingStatements.rationale: Warren's 'cost the limit of price' and Proudhon's cost-value are core mutualist principles that no current statement captures.
missingStatements.declined: Labour-cost pricing is specific to the mutualist and Warren tradition; the credit side is already covered and the bank should stay lean.

missingStatements.text: Borrowers should pay no more than the administrative cost of a loan, with no interest beyond that.
missingStatements.rationale: Proudhon proposed cutting the bank rate to administrative costs and eventually ending interest, and Tucker held that competition in credit would drive interest to cost.

notes: Proudhon's patriarchal views on women, family and divorce are not shared by Tucker or Greene, so these answers are low and split. Several answers on topics the sources never discuss (marked 0 or low) are inferred.
